b: The funding will support Ecostrat’s Canada Forest Innovation and Renewable Markets (FIRM) Challenge, which aims to connect investment-ready regions with international developers and investors to establish facilities that convert local organic waste and surplus biomass into low-carbon fuels, energy, chemicals and other materials.
Canada’s forest sector contributed $29.7bn to the country’s GDP in 2025 (Image: Unsplash)
The Canadian government has announced $2.2m in funding for an initiative to develop new markets and attract investment in the country’s forest sector.

The funding was announced on 19 Nov 2026 by Corey Hogan, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, at Scaling Up Bio 2026, Canada’s annual industrial bioeconomy conference. It will support Ecostrat’s Canada Forest Innovation and Renewable Markets (FIRM) Challenge.

The initiative aims to establish a network of up to 15 certified Bioeconomy Development Opportunity (BDO) Zones across Canada. These are regions assessed for their readiness to host commercial-scale manufacturing facilities that convert locally available organic waste and surplus biomass into low-carbon fuels, energy, chemicals and other materials.

BDO Zone assessments evaluate factors including biomass availability, infrastructure and workforce capacity, providing potential investors with an overview of a region’s suitability for new industrial projects. Certification is intended to help attract private investment, support rural and remote economies and advance industrial decarbonisation.

Working with Global Affairs Canada and the Trade Commissioner Service, Ecostrat will connect the designated regions with international developers and investors. The initiative aims to generate more than $1bn in new market opportunities for Canadian forest products within two years.

“As demand grows for new kinds of sustainable and low-carbon forest products, Canada’s forest sector is uniquely positioned to grow, especially through the network of new international trade relationships we are building,” said Tim Hodgson, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

The FIRM Challenge supports a key recommendation of the Canadian Forest Sector Transformation Task Force and one of the pillars of the forthcoming Forest Sector Strategy for Canada: diversifying export markets and creating new opportunities for forest products.

The proposed strategy is backed by $6.5bn in funding announced in Budget 2026, which the government describes as the largest investment in the country’s forest sector to date. The funding builds on $2.9bn in federal measures introduced since Aug 2025 to help the industry and its workers respond to tariffs, changing market conditions and the impacts of climate change.
